1:
The Partnership of Henry and William
In the late 1970s, mechanical genius Henry Emily partners with charismatic businessman William Afton. Together, they establish Fredbear's Family Diner in New Harmony, Indiana.

  • Henry's Role: The creative force. He invents the revolutionary "Springlock Animatronics"—costumes that use a system of mechanical gears and locks, allowing them to be worn by performers or operate autonomously as robotic performers.
  • William's Role: The business administrator, investor, and financial operator. Behind his professional exterior lies an escalating, deeply pathological envy of Henry's creative talent and a growing fixation on death, legacy, and human emotion.

The Springlock Technology
Henry designs two flagship characters: Fredbear (a golden bear) and Spring Bonnie (a golden rabbit).

The Danger of Springlocks: The springlock mechanisms are notoriously unstable. If moisture, sudden movement, or a mechanical flaw triggers the locks while a human is inside, the packed robotic parts snap violently forward into their default positions, instantly crushing, impaling, and shredding the occupant.
2:
The First Murder: The Death of Charlotte Emily (1983)
As business expands, the duo opens the first iteration of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. Henry creates a security animatronic called the Security Puppet specifically to protect his young daughter, Charlotte (Charlie) Emily.

  • The Incident: On a rainy night, a group of children lock Charlie outside the establishment. William Afton drives up, spots the isolated and crying girl, and in a fit of jealous rage against Henry, murders Charlie in the alleyway before driving off.
  • The First Possession: The Security Puppet, attempting to fulfill its programming, goes out into the pouring rain to save Charlie. The water short-circuits its systems, causing it to collapse over Charlie's corpse in the alley. Charlie's soul binds with the Puppet through her intense agony and need for protection, becoming the first possessed animatronic.
3:
The Bite of '83 (1983)
Back at Fredbear's Family Diner, William Afton's youngest son (commonly referred to as the Crying Child or Evan Afton) suffers severe psychological trauma. He is terrified of the animatronics, a fear exacerbated by his older brother, Michael Afton, who relentlessly bullies him using a Foxy mask.

  • The Prank gone Wrong: On the Crying Child's birthday, Michael and his friends carry the screaming boy to the stage and force his head into the mouth of the performing animatronic, Fredbear.
  • The Bite: The moisture from the child's tears triggers the springlocks in Fredbear's jaw. The mouth snaps shut with crushing force, crushing the child's skull.
  • The Aftermath: The Crying Child is rushed to the hospital, slipping into a coma. Beside his hospital bed, Michael expresses profound regret. A voice (implied to be William or a manifestation of his grief/plushie) promises the boy: "You're broken. I will put you back together." The Crying Child dies shortly after, closing down Fredbear's Family Diner permanently.
4:
The Missing Children's Incident (MCI) — 1985
Following the closure of Fredbear's, focus shifts entirely to the corporate flagship: Freddy Fazbear's Pizza (the original 1985 location). William Afton's psychological descent accelerates after losing his youngest son. He becomes obsessed with the concept of immortality and the supernatural energy generated by extreme human suffering, later classified as Agony and Remnant.

  • The Date: June 26, 1985.
  • The Method: William dons the Spring Bonnie suit to gain the trust of young children visiting the pizzeria. He lures five children—Susie, Jeremy, Gabriel, Fritz, and Cassidy—into the safe room (a hidden room omitted from the animatronics' digital maps).
  • The Slaughter: William murders all five children. He hides their corpses inside the operational animatronics: Chica (Susie), Bonnie (Jeremy), Freddy (Gabriel), Foxy (Fritz), and the spare springlock suit, Golden Freddy (Cassidy).
  • The Awakening: The Puppet (Charlie), driven by an instinct to comfort the dead, guides the spirits of the murdered children, effectively "giving them life" by binding their souls to the metal hulls of the animatronics.
  • The Closure: Customers soon complain of a foul odor, blood, and mucus leaking from the eyes and mouths of the animatronics. The police arrest William Afton, but due to a lack of physical evidence (the bodies are never found), he is ultimately released. The restaurant is abandoned and boarded up.
5:
Circus Baby's Pizza World
Eager to conduct unchecked experiments on soul extraction and capture metrics, William Afton forms a shell company, Afton Robotics LLC, and designs a new line of advanced robots: the Funtime Animatronics.

  • The Hidden Purpose: These animatronics are secretly equipped with internal storage tanks, claw mechanisms, and tracking systems engineered explicitly to capture and kill children in isolation.
  • The Death of Elizabeth Afton: William warns his daughter, Elizabeth, to stay away from Circus Baby. Mesmerized by the robot, Elizabeth approaches Baby when she is alone. Circus Baby's automated ice cream dispenser lures her close, a mechanical claw extends from Baby's torso, pulls Elizabeth inside her internal structure, and crushes her to death.

The Scooping Incident (Sister Location)
Years later, a grown Michael Afton is sent by his father down into the subterranean facility to "find his sister" and "put her back together."

  • The Trap: The Funtime Animatronics plot against Michael. Led by Circus Baby, they tear themselves apart and combine their mechanical endoskeletons into a singular, amorphous metallic entity known as Ennard.
  • The Scooper: Ennard lures Michael into the Scooping Room, eviscerates his internal organs, and climbs inside Michael's hollowed-out skin to use him as a human disguise.
  • The Reanimation: Ennard is forced to abandon the rotting flesh. However, due to the high concentration of Remnant injected into Michael's body by the Scooper, his soul remains bound to his decaying flesh. He stands up, vowing to hunt down his father.
6:
The Toy Animatronics (FNAF 2)
In 1987, Fazbear Entertainment attempts a massive corporate rebrand. They open a brand-new, high-budget Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. The original characters are replaced by the high-tech Toy Animatronics equipped with facial recognition software tied to a criminal database.

  • The Second Missing Children's Incident (DCI): William Afton infiltrates the new location using a fake alias. Using the Golden Freddy suit, William lures and murders a second group of five children. The dynamic souls of these new victims corrupt the programming of the Toy animatronics.
  • The Bite of '87: As the situation spirals out of control, a daytime birthday party is scheduled. Security guard Jeremy Fitzgerald is assigned to day-shift. Mangle (or potentially another Toy animatronic) lunges forward and bites off Jeremy's frontal lobe.
  • The Fallout: Jeremy survives, but the public relations nightmare forces Fazbear Entertainment to scrap the expensive Toy animatronics completely. The location is shut down.
7:
The FNAF 1 Location
In the early 1990s, a cash-strapped Fazbear Entertainment reopens a downscaled version of the pizzeria utilizing the original building from 1985. Operating under the pseudonym Mike Schmidt, Michael Afton takes the night guard job to investigate the pizzerias and find clues about his father's whereabouts. During this era, the long-term head of security, Phone Guy, is killed by the possessed animatronics.

The Springlock Trap (The "Follow Me" Minigames)
After the FNAF 1 location closes its doors for good due to bankruptcy, William Afton returns to the abandoned, rotting building to harvest the possessed metal.

  • The Destruction: Over several nights, William ambushes Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy one by one, dismantling them.
  • The Retribution: By destroying the physical hulls, William inadvertently releases the spirits of the five children. The ghosts corner William inside the hidden, leaking Safe Room.
  • The Birth of Springtrap: Terrified, William slides inside the old Spring Bonnie suit thinking he is safe. Rain dripping from the decaying roof leaks directly onto him. The moisture triggers the old springlocks. The mechanical parts snap shut, piercing William's flesh and shattering his bones. The Safe Room is sealed shut with William's trapped, corpse-fused body left inside to rot for thirty years.
8:
Fazbear's Fright (FNAF 3)
Thirty years after the closure, an independent group builds Fazbear's Fright: The Horror Attraction. They discover the mummified, springlocked corpse of William Afton, who is now Springtrap. At the end of the week, the attraction is burned to the ground. Springtrap survives the fire (becoming Scraptrap).

Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator (FNAF 6)
Henry Emily returns from hiding and designs a massive, final trap. He creates a fake Fazbear franchise location with an inescapable subterranean labyrinth. He lures the remaining possessed entities to the site: Scraptrap, Scrap Baby, Molten Freddy, and Lefty.

The Ultimate Fire: Henry overrides the facility controls and seals all exits. He sets the facility ablaze. Michael Afton chooses to stay and die in the fire. Henry dies alongside his creations. Elizabeth, Charlie, and the original 1985 souls are released to peace. Henry condemns William Afton to the deepest pits of hell.

Ultimate Custom Night (UCN)
One specific vengeful soul—Cassidy / Andrew—holds William back. The vengeful spirit constructs an eternal, shifting nightmare realm inside William's subconscious, subjecting him to an endless loop of being hunted and slaughtered by his past creations.
9:
Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted (The VR Game)
A corporate revival of Fazbear Entertainment commissions a Virtual Reality game. To save time, developers scan old animatronic circuit boards. One belongs to an ancient endoskeleton designed to mimic human behavior (The Mimic).

  • The Birth of Glitchtrap: The digital scan accidentally uploads the Mimic's programming—which had observed Afton's horrific acts—into the game's code. This manifests as a digital entity: Glitchtrap.
  • The Corruption of Vanessa: A beta tester named Vanessa is targeted. The virus manipulates her mind, creating a secondary, murderous persona within her: Vanny.

Security Breach & Ruin
Fazbear Entertainment opens the Freddy Fazbear Mega Pizzaplex. Vanny uses the Pizzaplex resources to construct a flesh-and-metal fusion body for the trapped physical Mimic endoskeleton (manifesting as Burntrap), and spreads a virus throughout the network. A homeless youth named Gregory gets trapped overnight, teams up with Glamrock Freddy, and dismantles the corrupted Glamrock animatronics to escape.
10:
The Modern Context of Oswald
Decades after the closure of the original 1985 pizzerias, a young boy named Oswald discovers an old, dirty ballpit inside Jeff's Pizza—which is structurally built directly on top of the original boarded-up 1985 Freddy Fazbear's Pizza location.

  • The Agony Matrix: The ballpit acts as a physical conduit for Agony. The pure emotional horror generated by William Afton's slaughter of the five children on June 26, 1985, became physically embedded into the environment, creating a pocket dimension or a chronological echo.
  • The Encounter with the Yellow Rabbit: When Oswald submerges himself, he is pulled back through time into a vivid loop of the 1985 tragedy. The primary antagonist is not Afton, but a demonic amalgamation known as the Yellow Rabbit (Pit Bonnie) birthed purely from concentrated Agony.
  • The Resolution: The Yellow Rabbit escapes into the modern day, dragging Oswald's father into the pit. Oswald fights back, returns to the ballpit dimension, and manages to hang the entity, suffocating it into dust and freeing his real father.
Summary Conclusion: Into the Pit proves that even if physical animatronics are burned, the Agony of William Afton’s initial 1985 murders remains permanently anchored to the earth, capable of manifesting new nightmares independent of Afton's living soul.
